# open-ferry-ai-proxy

> Open Ferry is a local AI proxy, a Rust port of CLIProxyAPI. On one port (8317 by default) it serves OpenAI Chat Completions and Responses, Claude Messages and the Gemini API, and passes each request on to an account or API key from its config: Codex and Claude sign-ins, the user's own Claude Code, Gemini, Vertex AI, xAI and OpenAI-compatible upstreams. It reads CLIProxyAPI's config.yaml and auth directory as they are. Pre-alpha: the first release, 0.1.0, isn't out yet, and the releases before it are candidates for it.

Start with the README's Quick start: install with a published candidate's install script, create a config and add an OpenAI-compatible API-key provider, connect a tool with the local base URL and client key, and verify a model reply with curl. Candidates 0.0.3 and 0.0.4 are published; the container image comes with the first release. docs/agents.md has the other provider and client setups. To replace a CLIProxyAPI setup instead, on its own config and credentials, run `open-ferry migrate` after installing; it asks before it changes anything, `-dry-run` only shows the plan, and `open-ferry migrate -undo` switches back. Clients send a client key from the config's `access.api-keys`; the management API at `/v0/management/` takes the config's `management.secret-key`. Both keys are secrets: keep them out of logs and commits.

To look at a setup or change it, use Open Ferry's own commands, `open-ferry status`, `config`, `keys`, `credentials` and `clients` (with `--json`), or its MCP server, `open-ferry mcp`, rather than editing the YAML or calling the management API with curl: they check each change, mask every secret in what they print, never take a secret as an argument, and change nothing risky without `--yes` (`confirm: true` for a tool).

## Docs

- [Setup for coding agents](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Loft-902-Co-LLC/open-ferry-ai-proxy/main/docs/agents.md): install, `open-ferry init` and `check`, where the config lives, looking at and changing a setup with the commands or the MCP server, pointing Codex, Claude Code and OpenAI-compatible clients at the proxy, and the management API
- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Loft-902-Co-LLC/open-ferry-ai-proxy/main/README.md): the four-step quick start, installation alternatives, building from source, the dashboard, and parity with CLIProxyAPI
- [Feature inventory](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Loft-902-Co-LLC/open-ferry-ai-proxy/main/docs/features.md): the full ported endpoint, provider, routing, management and translation inventory, moved from the README Status section
- [The command line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Loft-902-Co-LLC/open-ferry-ai-proxy/main/docs/cli.md): `open-ferry init`, `check`, `service`, `update` and `migrate`, and `status`, `config`, `keys`, `credentials`, `clients` and `mcp`, in full: flags, output, exit codes and what needs `--yes`
- [The MCP server](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Loft-902-Co-LLC/open-ferry-ai-proxy/main/docs/mcp.md): `open-ferry mcp`'s tools, what needs `confirm: true`, and adding it to Claude Code, Codex, T3 Code or Cursor
- [Updates](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Loft-902-Co-LLC/open-ferry-ai-proxy/main/docs/updates.md): how Open Ferry keeps itself up to date with `open-ferry update`, what it downloads and how often, signed releases, rollback, and every way to turn updates off
- [Migrating from CLIProxyAPI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Loft-902-Co-LLC/open-ferry-ai-proxy/main/docs/migrating-from-cliproxyapi.md): `open-ferry migrate`, which switches a CLIProxyAPI setup to open-ferry and back (`migrate -undo`), and what carries over from a CLIProxyAPI setup and what doesn't
- [The config template](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Loft-902-Co-LLC/open-ferry-ai-proxy/main/config.example.yaml): every setting, with comments and commented examples of each provider

## APIs

- [The dashboard API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Loft-902-Co-LLC/open-ferry-ai-proxy/main/docs/dashboard-api.md): `/open-ferry/api/v1/`, for usage, request-log search and ready-made client setups, and how both it and the management API check the management key
- [UPSTREAM.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Loft-902-Co-LLC/open-ferry-ai-proxy/main/UPSTREAM.md): what was ported from CLIProxyAPI v8.0.38, including the management API routes, and every deliberate difference

## Optional

- [Claude through your own Claude Code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Loft-902-Co-LLC/open-ferry-ai-proxy/main/docs/claude-subscription.md): the `claude-cli` entries, and why the Claude sign-in goes against Anthropic's terms
- [Routing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Loft-902-Co-LLC/open-ferry-ai-proxy/main/docs/routing.md): how a credential is picked, Open Ferry's `quota` strategy and its cap on long quota rests (`routing.quota`)
- [Benchmarks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Loft-902-Co-LLC/open-ferry-ai-proxy/main/docs/benchmarks.md): Open Ferry against CLIProxyAPI in front of the same fake upstream, and how to rerun it
- [Changelog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Loft-902-Co-LLC/open-ferry-ai-proxy/main/CHANGELOG.md): what is in place today
